summary.title: Hacking team communications
summary.one_liner: A engineering manager's approach to staying informed about team progress without standups or constant status-asking, using filtered email, Trello, GitHub notifications, shorter meetings, and habit-building with the team.
keywords: stay up to date with team progress
takeaways: Use email filters and inbox zero so only relevant messages demand attention.
Keep one Trello Kanban board per team with prioritized tickets and minimal items per list, and subscribe to board activity.
Watch GitHub repository activity and encourage opening draft PRs early to surface direction and get feedback sooner.
Make meetings shorter (e.g. 30 minutes), require agendas, and move to meetings only when email cannot resolve an issue.
Build team habits by explaining why communication matters, asking for brief replies like 'still in progress', and gently reminding people to update tickets.
summary.summary: The author, an engineering manager, describes how to keep up with a team's progress without constant status checks or standups. The post covers four channels: email (filters and inbox zero, turning ongoing items into tickets), Trello (a single Kanban board with prioritized tickets and notifications), GitHub (repository subscriptions, in-app notifications, and early draft PRs), and meetings (preferring email, requiring agendas, and shortening meeting length). It ends with how to build team communication habits through explanation, short acknowledgements, and friendly reminders.
